label: start
name: starting architecture
last_analysis: All 9 trials scored exactly 0, on dev and on training success. That covers different heads (pooled, footprint-window, per-layer, dense, attention), different recipes and different horizons. Because the network made no difference, I suspect one cause affects every trial. My best guess is that the policy collapses to calling DONE. Random placements mostly fill cells outside the target, so their reward is negative (about -0.09 per step), while DONE gives 0. The DONE logit gains early, episodes get short, and the agent rarely samples the good placements it needs to learn from. Normalised advantages and an entropy coefficient of 0.01 do little to stop this. I could not observe this directly; it is an inference. The last round tests remedies for this collapse: a high entropy bonus, a longer discount horizon so that future positive placements outweigh stopping, and a DONE logit that learns more slowly. Two use the cheap baseline network and one uses the window head, which had the most detailed per-placement view of the cells.
